attempted_claim: With the same alpha=1.25, K_alpha=SO(3) union alpha*SO(3) and exponent p=2, consider homogeneous W^{1,2} gradient Young measures nu supported on K_alpha with barycenter bar(nu)=t0*I_3 where t0=(1+alpha)/2. Decide claim S3: every such nu is a finite-order laminate (a hierarchic rank-one splitting supported on pairwise rank-one connected matrices with centre t0*I_3), so no non-laminate zero-energy microstructure exists at this hydrostatic barycenter. A complete answer either proves S3 by deriving laminate representation from Jensen inequalities for all quasiconvex functions plus rank-one compatibility analysis of K_alpha, or disproves S3 by constructing an explicit homogeneous gradient Young measure supported on K_alpha with barycenter t0*I_3 and proving it is generated by gradients of a bounded W^{1,2} sequence yet is not a finite-order laminate (e.g. via a nontrivial quasiconvex Jensen gap or Kinderlehrer-Pedregal characterization failure).
decisive_failure: originality: The exact headline (alpha=1.25, barycenter 9/8 I, no homogeneous W^{1,2} gradient Young measure on SO(3) U 1.25 SO(3)) is substantively implied by stronger published results, so it is a corollary/recomputation rather than a new claim. Ball-James 2015 proves general incompatibility of dilatational wells k1 SO(3), k2 SO(3) for compact disjoint k1,k2 with p-transfer via Lemma 1, instantiated at {1},{1.25}; Zhang 1997 Thm 1.1 (n>=2, body-verified) gives QCH(SO(3))=SO(3), which by dilation-invariance excludes 9/8 I from each single well. Their conjunction implies the headline. D-K-M-S 2000 scope, delimited via body-inspected Ball-James account, is restricted sufficient conditions and does not itself cover this dilatational pair. value: Although the TARGET S3 question is proved in vacuous form by a correct short argument at a motivated symmetric midpoint, the exact datum is mechanically implied by the stronger recorded dilatational-incompatibility plus single-well-hull theorems, so it fails the 'not known or mechanically implied' condition for a narrow exact invariant. Instantiating a general published rigidity result at {1},{1.25} plus standard scaling adds no independent retrieval value beyond citing those stronger facts, even though the elementary cof-at-p=2 route is elegant.
